chapter: Young Excelsior and the old-time band scene
title: Old-style bands versus new music; white Dixieland bands; lost organized bands
summary: Robertson says he and the band will back a leader sticking to the old style, comments on white Dixieland bands on Bourbon Street, and laments that bands are no longer organized or steady.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Is jazz healthy? Young players, rock and the future

blocks.x: They want us to get together. And as soon as he can get straight, we going on with him. We ain't gonna take nothing but an old set up. The old style of band. The old set up. Well, if we going on with him, if he falls, we fall too. That's what we figured. If he make it, we make it. And if he don't, well, none of us make it. That's our idea, going along with him. Because he got confidence in us. It's one thing anywhere he put us, we gonna wait. And if it's money there, he'll get it. Because we can wait. If we live, we'll wait. And we're gonna try to put us up on the street, and we're gonna try to help him, and we're gonna help Buster. If he's got good confidence in Buster and he thinks that we can do it, we're gonna try to do it. Because you see all this new type of music now. It's all right for a while. It lasts for a while. But the people coming in now, you take all the northern people, they come here for that type of music. We got bands down there now. Down there, Brooke Carell down there playing on Boybin Street down there now. They have to get away from that new type of music. We don't have to fool ourselves. We got some white bands down there. Gives us plenty hell, white boys. Gives us plenty hell with that Dixieland music. Oh yeah. You see, they can't play. And they're not no old timers. They're young comers. They're part of the gift. Gives us plenty of things. That Dixieland music. That's right. Because the type of music we were playing, the average fellow was playing, they went jump up and left it and went full with this new type of music. And those boys that went on with that, picked up that old time music and went in that old time music, sent them big. And they're on the radio. Yeah, they're on the radio. And they can play it too. Man that's blowing, they can play it. Lots of times I yell on the radio, I said, the time they yell on the radio, I have to shake my head. And one of them is Joe Oliver or Lewis Armstrong. Which one of them is playing? You know, boys right down there. Now you tell, you take this boy, what you call them down there. You got one of the best bands down there in that place. And them colored boys down there, they got to play. You take Sharky, Sharky got a band. And they put bands. They got a good band. We got another fellow down there. They go put it on there playing down there. Sure. You boys and men can play. You see? They have a good band. But now coming out of the brass band, the old time bands here. We don't have no more old time bands. You don't have no more left nines. You have the Herica band. You have the John Kazmi that there, Young Tuxedo. Now you ain't got no more organized band outside Young Excelsior. Now you don't have no organized bands. Old bands. Those bands are only made up bands. Yeah. They make up. They don't have no more study bands like they used to. You see one time you could get out there, you'd hire a band, you'd see that same face today you see tomorrow, you see it the next day. If you hire them for a week, you'd see that same ten faces out there, but you can't do it now. Because they're not organized like they used to. Years ago they're not organized.
